And so, as you can see, there is a lot of corruption going on. Something called simony where positions in the Catholic Church can be bought and sold, very similar to the imperial bureaucracy of China. Priests are not really divine; they get married, and their positions are often sold to nobles. Kings can appoint leaders of the church as well. There is this negotiation going on between the Catholic Church and the kings. Parishioners, no matter how poor they are, are forced to pay a tax to the Catholic Church and not to the king.

The king is not happy about this because a third of his land and most of his tax revenue is being taken over by the Catholic Church. This leads to rebellions against the Catholic Church. The church controls one-third of all land in Europe, tax-free, leading to feudalism. Despite its power, the Catholic Church has legitimacy problems. Muslims occupy the Holy Land; if you truly represent God, why is Jerusalem in Muslim hands? Spain is part of Europe but Muslim Spain is much more wealthy and innovative than the rest of Europe. In 1054, the Eastern Orthodox Church led by the Byzantines breaks with the Catholic Church because both want to be the ultimate center of the world—Byzantines say they are the center, Romans claim otherwise. There's corruption within the church, leading to rebellions from religious leaders who want to unleash a divine spark.

There are different solutions to these legitimacy problems. One solution is that the Catholic Church persecutes Jews, allowing them to exist so the church can scapegoat them. Throughout this time, Jews are being persecuted mainly by being forced out of their homes where they lived for hundreds of years and expelled from regions. This is shown in a map of Jewish persecution, with black spots indicating areas of massacres.

The map also shows Christian pilgrimages to the holy land, which is a source of embarrassment since Jerusalem is occupied by Muslims and Christians have to pay taxes to them. Currently, the Holy Land, Jerusalem, is controlled by the Ottoman Empire.

Pope Urban II eventually calls for the crusades to liberate the holy land from Muslims. He says that those who die in the crusades, whether by land or sea or in battle against pagans, will have immediate remission of sins. If you fight the demons, it doesn't matter who you are; even poor people and sinners have an opportunity to go to heaven.

So Pope Urban II is calling for the crusades to fight the demons.
